project.name: sil
project.description: SiL framework for deterministic scheduling and typed data routing in vECU simulation.

nodes.name: arena.h
nodes.summary: Defines the fixed-layout shared-memory arena contract for transporting channel payloads between the kernel and process participants. Its sequence and length fields provide freshness and payload-size metadata without depending on the step protocol.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a C-compatible packed-by-convention POD layout that is shared by C and C++ code.

nodes.name: clock_region.h
nodes.summary: Defines the fixed-layout shared region used to publish frozen virtual time and realtime epoch values from the kernel to the clock shim. It is the C-compatible contract between the writer and preloaded reader.
nodes.languageNotes: Exposes a stable two-field nanosecond layout through extern-C-compatible declarations.

nodes.name: clock_shim.cpp
nodes.summary: Locates the clock-shim shared library next to the running sil executable, with platform-specific library names and executable-path discovery. The resolved path is reused when shimmed participants are spawned.

nodes.name: clock_shim.hpp
nodes.summary: Declares the kernel-facing helper that resolves the absolute path of the virtual clock preload library shipped beside the runner.

nodes.name: mapped_region.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements RAII ownership of filesystem-backed shared mappings, including temporary-file creation, sizing, mmap setup, move transfer, and complete release. Failures are reported through an error string and clean up partial resources.

nodes.name: mapped_region.hpp
nodes.summary: Defines the move-only MappedRegion RAII abstraction used to own a mapped temporary file, its descriptor, and its filesystem path for the lifetime of a shared-memory region.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses move-only ownership so exactly one object is responsible for unmapping, closing, and unlinking the backing file.

nodes.name: process_participant.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements the sequential subprocess participant endpoint, including JSON-lines handshaking, deterministic input/output ordering, base64 and arena transport, virtual-clock injection, process I/O, and shutdown. It connects Engine queues to an external process while enforcing manifest and transport invariants.

nodes.name: process_participant.hpp
nodes.summary: Declares the ProcessParticipant endpoint and its state for deterministic subprocess execution, including Engine queue bindings, shared clock and arena mappings, protocol I/O, and step-scoped codecs.

nodes.name: clock_shim.c
nodes.summary: Implements the preloadable virtual-clock shim that maps the shared clock region and interposes POSIX clock and sleep APIs. It serves stepped virtual time when configured and falls back to the real libc functions when the region is unavailable.
nodes.languageNotes: Provides separate macOS interpose-table and Linux LD_PRELOAD implementations, with lazy libc symbol lookup on Linux.

nodes.name: runner_dir
nodes.summary: Finds and canonicalizes the directory containing the running sil executable, using Mach-O APIs on macOS and /proc/self/exe on other platforms.

nodes.name: clock_shim_library_path
nodes.summary: Builds the platform-specific absolute path to the clock-shim shared library beside the runner, returning an empty path when runner discovery fails.

nodes.name: ~MappedRegion
nodes.summary: Releases the mapped region and all of its owned operating-system resources during destruction.

nodes.name: MappedRegion
nodes.summary: Transfers mapping ownership from another MappedRegion and clears the moved-from object's descriptor, path, base pointer, and size.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Creates a named temporary file, sizes it, and maps it read/write with MAP_SHARED, returning an empty region and an explanatory error after any failed setup step.

nodes.name: release
nodes.summary: Unmaps the region, closes its descriptor, unlinks its backing file, and resets ownership state so cleanup is idempotent.

nodes.name: MappedRegion
nodes.summary: Declares the default construction of an initially empty MappedRegion owner.

nodes.name: MappedRegion
nodes.summary: Move-only RAII abstraction for a shared memory mapping backed by a temporary filesystem file. It exposes creation, mapping access, and path inspection while ensuring destruction releases the mapping, descriptor, and directory entry.

nodes.name: b64_encode
nodes.summary: Encodes a byte vector into standard base64 text for inline participant protocol messages.

nodes.name: b64_decode
nodes.summary: Decodes base64 message data into bytes, rejecting invalid symbols with a RunError.

nodes.name: ProcessParticipant::StepCodec
nodes.summary: Private step-protocol codec that selects arena transport for the first message on an arena-backed channel and inline base64 transport for subsequent or non-arena messages. It decodes each output according to the transport field actually present on the wire.

nodes.name: StepCodec
nodes.summary: Initializes a step codec with the owning ProcessParticipant and its arena adapter.

nodes.name: encode_inputs
nodes.summary: Encodes ordered step inputs as JSON, using one arena reference for the first message per arena-backed channel and inline base64 for the rest.

nodes.name: decode_outputs
nodes.summary: Decodes participant output messages into typed step outputs, honoring each item's shm_seq or inline data representation.

nodes.name: setup_clock_region
nodes.summary: Creates and initializes the participant's shared virtual-clock region, then resolves the preload library path before forking.

nodes.name: inject_shim_env
nodes.summary: Sets the shared clock-region path and platform-specific preload variable in the forked child before exec.

nodes.name: write_clock_region
nodes.summary: Publishes the current virtual step time into the mapped clock region, doing nothing for unshimmed participants.

nodes.name: setup_arenas
nodes.summary: Validates arena-backed channel directions and creates one sized shared mapping for every subscribed or published shared-memory channel.

nodes.name: write_arena
nodes.summary: Writes a payload into a channel arena after capacity validation and increments its sequence marker.

nodes.name: read_arena
nodes.summary: Reads an arena payload after checking sequence freshness and capacity bounds, raising RunError for stale or invalid data.

nodes.name: ProcessParticipant
nodes.summary: Builds a process participant, binds its Engine inputs, prepares optional clock and arena mappings, forks and execs the child, and completes the JSON-lines init/ready handshake.

nodes.name: ~ProcessParticipant
nodes.summary: Delegates participant destruction to the shutdown path so child-process and descriptor cleanup occurs before object release.

nodes.name: step
nodes.summary: Collects visible Engine messages in global publish order, sends one deterministic step request at the current virtual time, validates the response, and publishes decoded outputs.

nodes.name: send_line
nodes.summary: Writes a newline-terminated protocol line completely to the child stdin, retrying partial writes and raising RunError on failure.

nodes.name: read_line
nodes.summary: Buffers child stdout until a complete newline-delimited protocol message is available and reports unexpected child termination as RunError.

nodes.name: shutdown
nodes.summary: Performs best-effort protocol shutdown, closes child pipes, waits briefly for reaping, force-kills if necessary, and releases all shared regions.

nodes.name: ProcessParticipant
nodes.summary: Declares construction of a process participant from an Engine, participant name, and process specification.

nodes.name: ProcessParticipant
nodes.summary: Represents a sequential external-process endpoint that exchanges step messages with the Engine and owns its child-process, protocol, virtual-clock, and channel-arena state.

nodes.name: sil_clock_shim_init
nodes.summary: Runs at library load to map the read-only shared clock region named by SIL_CLOCK_REGION and records its address for hot-path clock reads.

nodes.name: is_monotonic
nodes.summary: Classifies supported clock IDs as monotonic virtual-time clocks versus realtime-class clocks.

nodes.name: engine.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements the deterministic simulation engine: participant setup, task registration, virtual-time scheduling, channel publication, and shutdown. It applies channel interceptors and routes surviving messages to subscribers and recording sinks.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses C++ callbacks, stable registration indices, and explicit virtual-time slots to make scheduling order deterministic.

nodes.name: interceptor.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements runtime evaluation of compiled channel interceptor plans. It applies drop decisions, saturating delays, duration truncation, and in-place byte overrides in a fixed order.

nodes.name: interceptor.hpp
nodes.summary: Declares the compiled interceptor-plan abstraction used by the engine for per-channel message decisions. The interface documents ordering, time-window semantics, saturation, and override safety guarantees.

nodes.name: manifest.cpp
nodes.summary: Loads and validates the JSON simulation manifest, including schemas, channels, interceptors, and native, process, or replay participants. It computes the manifest hash and compiles validated interceptor declarations into runtime plans.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses canonical JSON and name-sorted object iteration so manifest-derived layouts, hashes, and registration order remain stable.

nodes.name: recording_reader.hpp
nodes.summary: Defines the format-neutral recording reader seam. Readers expose embedded channel schemas and consume recorded messages in total publish order, while replay-specific verification remains in the replayer.

nodes.name: replayer.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements replay participant construction and timestamped message injection. It verifies recording hashes and schemas, filters selected channels, and publishes due messages through the engine in recorded order.

nodes.name: replayer.hpp
nodes.summary: Declares the scheduled replay participant and its two engine-facing operations: reporting the next recorded timestamp and publishing messages due at a virtual-time slot.

nodes.name: sha256.hpp
nodes.summary: Provides a self-contained SHA-256 implementation and a string-to-hex convenience function for manifest and recording integrity checks. The header avoids platform crypto dependencies so hashes are portable across runtimes.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements the FIPS 180-4 block schedule and compression rounds directly in header-only C++.

nodes.name: Engine
nodes.summary: Constructs engine channel state from the validated manifest and clones each channel's compiled interceptor plan for runtime use.

nodes.name: setup
nodes.summary: Instantiates native, replay, and process participants, rejects live/replay channel collisions, and registers process step callbacks before the run begins.

nodes.name: register_task
nodes.summary: Validates a task period and records its deterministic name, timing, priority, registration index, callback, and completion state.

nodes.name: publish
nodes.summary: Validates a channel payload, applies its interceptor plan, records surviving messages, and fans them out to subscriber queues.

nodes.name: take
nodes.summary: Returns the next queued message only when its latency-adjusted visibility time has been reached.

nodes.name: fail
nodes.summary: Captures the first participant failure as engine state so the scheduler can stop the run with a deterministic error.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Advances virtual time to the next task or replay slot, orders due tasks by priority and registration, injects replay messages, and shuts down processes after completion.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Evaluates an interceptor plan in order, suppressing drops and out-of-duration messages, composing saturating delays, and applying safe byte overrides.

nodes.name: InterceptorPlan
nodes.summary: Encapsulates the compiled steps and duration boundary for one channel's runtime message transformation policy.

nodes.name: parse_schema
nodes.summary: Validates schema field declarations, rejects unknown or duplicate fields, and computes the schema's serialized byte width and canonical JSON.

nodes.name: encode_override
nodes.summary: Converts an override constant into little-endian bytes for unsigned, signed, or floating-point field layouts, clamping integer bounds as needed.

nodes.name: parse_interceptors
nodes.summary: Validates channel interceptor declarations, time windows, drop parameters, delays, and scalar override values against the channel schema.

nodes.name: parse_participant
nodes.summary: Parses native, process, and replay participant specifications while validating commands, timing, shim options, and referenced channels.

nodes.name: compile_interceptor_plan
nodes.summary: Transforms validated interceptor specifications into runtime steps with compiled kinds, time windows, parameters, and schema-relative override offsets.

nodes.name: load_manifest
nodes.summary: Reads and validates a manifest JSON document, computes its content hash and base directory, builds schemas and channels, compiles interceptors, and parses participants.

nodes.name: RecordingReader
nodes.summary: Defines the abstract read-side recording contract, including embedded channel schemas and one-shot transfer of messages in stored publish order.

nodes.name: Replayer
nodes.summary: Loads and hashes a recording, validates selected channel schemas, filters messages by channel and run duration, and stores them for scheduled replay.

nodes.name: next_publish_ns
nodes.summary: Reports the next queued recording timestamp, or the maximum timestamp sentinel when replay is exhausted.

nodes.name: publish_due
nodes.summary: Publishes every queued message whose timestamp equals the current virtual time, preserving the recording's stored order.

nodes.name: Replayer
nodes.summary: Models a deterministic replay participant whose messages enter the engine at recorded virtual timestamps before task activation.

nodes.name: update
nodes.summary: Feeds arbitrary bytes into the SHA-256 state and compresses each complete 64-byte block.

nodes.name: hex_digest
nodes.summary: Finalizes the SHA-256 stream with padding and length encoding, then formats the digest as lowercase hexadecimal text.

nodes.name: process_block
nodes.summary: Executes the SHA-256 message schedule and 64-round compression function for one input block.

nodes.name: Sha256
nodes.summary: Maintains incremental SHA-256 state, buffered input, and block-processing helpers for portable integrity hashing.

nodes.name: sha256_hex
nodes.summary: Hashes a complete string with Sha256 and returns its hexadecimal digest.

nodes.name: engine.hpp
nodes.summary: Declares the deterministic simulation engine, subscriber queues, pending messages, and participant-facing runtime services. It defines the virtual-time scheduling and publish/take interface shared by native, process, and replay adapters.
nodes.languageNotes: C++ header combines inline queue semantics with opaque participant forward declarations and an engine implementation seam.

nodes.name: main.cpp
nodes.summary: CLI entry point for sil-run. It parses the manifest and output arguments, validates optional clock-shim availability, selects a recording sink, runs the engine, and maps configuration or runtime failures to exit codes.

nodes.name: manifest.hpp
nodes.summary: Defines the typed in-memory manifest model used to configure schemas, channels, fault interceptors, and native, process, or replay participants. It also exposes manifest loading and channel lookup declarations.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses C++17 optional, variant, filesystem, and shared ownership to represent heterogeneous participant and transport configuration.

nodes.name: mcap_recording.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements MCAP recording and replay-reader factories. The recorder embeds manifest-derived schemas and channels while preserving publish order; the reader validates an MCAP file and materializes format-neutral schemas and messages for replay.
nodes.languageNotes: Defines MCAP_IMPLEMENTATION in one translation unit and keeps the rest of the kernel dependent on format-neutral recording interfaces.

nodes.name: mcap_recording.hpp
nodes.summary: Declares the MCAP-backed RecordingSink implementation, including its writer, channel-ID mapping, and idempotent close state.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a forward declaration and unique_ptr for the external MCAP writer so consumers only see the recording abstraction.

nodes.name: recording_sink.hpp
nodes.summary: Defines the format-neutral recording seam consumed by the engine and the factory that selects a concrete sink from an output path.

nodes.name: RunError
nodes.summary: Runtime error type for failures while executing an otherwise valid manifest.

nodes.name: PendingMessage
nodes.summary: Carries a published payload together with its visibility timestamp and global publish sequence for deterministic queue ordering.

nodes.name: SubQueue
nodes.summary: Maintains one subscriber's FIFO view of a channel and exposes latency-aware visibility, sequence inspection, enqueue, and dequeue operations.

nodes.name: Engine
nodes.summary: Coordinates manifest setup, participant task registration, virtual-time execution, channel publication, subscriptions, recording, and failure propagation.

nodes.name: visible_at
nodes.summary: Checks whether the front pending message is visible at a virtual timestamp, applying explicit latency or next-activation semantics while preserving strict FIFO order.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Parses sil-run arguments, loads and validates the manifest, creates the selected recorder, executes setup and runtime, and reports configuration or execution failures.

nodes.name: ManifestError
nodes.summary: Configuration error type used when a manifest or recording configuration cannot be accepted by the runner.

nodes.name: FieldSpec
nodes.summary: Describes a typed schema field and its optional fixed-size array cardinality.

nodes.name: SchemaSpec
nodes.summary: Stores schema fields, canonical JSON, and the packed byte size used for message validation and recording.

nodes.name: InterceptorSpec
nodes.summary: Represents a manifest-declared channel fault such as drop, drop_nth, delay, or field override over a time window.

nodes.name: ChannelSpec
nodes.summary: Defines a channel's schema, latency, transport mode, declared interceptors, and compiled interceptor plan.

nodes.name: NativeSpec
nodes.summary: Configures a native participant library and its JSON configuration payload.

nodes.name: ProcessSpec
nodes.summary: Configures a process participant's command, period, channel subscriptions/publications, priority, and optional virtual clock shim.

nodes.name: ReplaySpec
nodes.summary: Configures a recording file, expected content hash, and channels to replay.

nodes.name: ParticipantSpec
nodes.summary: Associates a participant name with a variant containing native, process, or replay implementation details.

nodes.name: Manifest
nodes.summary: Top-level execution configuration containing duration, epoch, schemas, sorted channels and participants, manifest hash, and base directory.

nodes.name: McapRecorder
nodes.summary: Opens an MCAP writer, records the manifest hash, and registers manifest schemas and channels in deterministic order.

nodes.name: record
nodes.summary: Converts a published kernel message into an MCAP message using the manifest channel mapping, sequence number, timestamp, and payload bytes.

nodes.name: make_recording_sink
nodes.summary: Selects and constructs the MCAP recording sink for .mcap output, rejecting unsupported extensions as manifest errors.

nodes.name: McapRecordingReader
nodes.summary: Private format-neutral reader that validates MCAP schemas and channels, snapshots messages in file order, and exposes them to replay code.

nodes.name: McapRecordingReader
nodes.summary: Loads an MCAP file, validates its summary and schema references, and buffers channel schemas and messages for stable replay iteration.

nodes.name: make_recording_reader
nodes.summary: Constructs an MCAP recording reader for .mcap paths and rejects unsupported recording formats.

nodes.name: McapRecorder
nodes.summary: RecordingSink implementation that owns an MCAP writer, maps manifest channel indices to MCAP IDs, and tracks idempotent closure.

nodes.name: RecordingSink
nodes.summary: Abstract format-neutral interface for recording published messages and finalizing a recording exactly once.

nodes.name: participant.h
nodes.summary: Defines the stable C ABI contract for native SiL participants, including task registration, channel subscription, message transfer, virtual-time access, and run failure reporting.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses extern "C" guards and function pointers so C++ kernel code can load participant libraries through a stable C ABI.

nodes.name: sil_participant_init
nodes.summary: Declares the shared-library entry point that receives the ABI table and manifest configuration during participant startup.

nodes.name: native_participant.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements the native participant adapter that exposes the C ABI to shared libraries and forwards setup, data-plane, timing, and failure operations into the engine.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses dlopen and dlsym for runtime library loading while converting C++ exceptions into Engine::fail diagnostics at the ABI boundary.

nodes.name: NativeApiBridge
nodes.summary: Provides the static callback table used to bridge native participant calls into the engine through a NativeParticipant context.

nodes.name: register_task
nodes.summary: Validates setup-time task registration requests, adapts the C callback signature, and registers the task with the engine.

nodes.name: subscribe
nodes.summary: Validates a setup-time channel subscription and stores the engine-owned subqueue for later message retrieval.

nodes.name: publish
nodes.summary: Checks task-context validity and forwards a participant message to the engine's publish path, routing failures through the engine diagnostic channel.

nodes.name: take
nodes.summary: Retrieves the next visible message from a subscribed channel, copies it into participant-owned temporary storage, and returns its data and length through the C ABI.

nodes.name: now_ns
nodes.summary: Returns the engine's current stepped virtual time in nanoseconds to a native participant.

nodes.name: fail
nodes.summary: Reports a participant failure to the engine, substituting a default diagnostic when the reason is null.

nodes.name: NativeParticipant
nodes.summary: Loads a participant shared library, resolves its initialization entry point, constructs the ABI callback table, and invokes participant initialization with manifest configuration.

nodes.name: ~NativeParticipant
nodes.summary: Releases the dynamically loaded participant library handle when the adapter is destroyed.

nodes.name: native_participant.hpp
nodes.summary: Declares the NativeParticipant engine adapter and its state for a loaded library, ABI table, channel subscriptions, and temporary message storage.

nodes.name: NativeParticipant
nodes.summary: Owns the lifetime and engine-facing state of one dynamically loaded native participant, including its subscriptions and ABI bridge context.

nodes.name: NativeParticipant
nodes.summary: Declares construction of a native participant adapter from an engine, participant specification, name, and base directory.

nodes.name: toy_accumulator.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements a toy native participant that consumes toy.Counter messages and publishes a running toy.Accum count and sum on each activation.

nodes.name: Accumulator
nodes.summary: Stores the accumulator participant's ABI pointer, input and output channels, and running count and sum state.

nodes.name: accumulate
nodes.summary: Drains visible input messages, updates the running count and sum, and publishes the resulting aggregate message.

nodes.name: sil_participant_init
nodes.summary: Parses accumulator configuration, binds its channels and ABI table, subscribes to input, and registers the periodic accumulation task.

nodes.name: toy_producer.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements a toy native participant that emits sequenced toy.Counter messages at a configured periodic rate.

nodes.name: Producer
nodes.summary: Stores the producer participant's ABI pointer, destination channel, and monotonically increasing sequence number.

nodes.name: tick
nodes.summary: Builds the next toy.Counter payload, increments the producer sequence, publishes it, and reports publish failures through the participant API.

nodes.name: sil_participant_init
nodes.summary: Parses producer configuration, initializes its destination channel, and registers the periodic publishing task.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Python package entry point that re-exports the public manifest builder and manifest reference types.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses __all__ to define the package-level public API.

nodes.name: manifest.py
nodes.summary: Builds the declarative execution manifest consumed by the SiL kernel, validating schemas, channels, interceptors, and participants. It emits canonical JSON and computes a SHA-256 hash so simulation inputs remain deterministic.
nodes.languageNotes: Canonical JSON uses sorted keys and compact separators, while default-compatible fields are omitted to preserve historical hashes.

nodes.name: ManifestError
nodes.summary: ValueError subclass raised when a manifest declaration cannot be accepted as valid kernel input.

nodes.name: ManifestRef
nodes.summary: Frozen value object carrying the path and content hash returned after writing a manifest.

nodes.name: Manifest
nodes.summary: Primary manifest builder that registers message schemas, channels, fault interceptors, and native, process, or replay participants. It validates cross-references, serializes the canonical run document, hashes it, and writes it to disk.

nodes.name: participant.py
nodes.summary: Implements the Python endpoint for SiL's JSON-line step protocol, including inline and shared-memory payload transport, participant lifecycle dispatch, and dynamic participant loading.
nodes.languageNotes: The endpoint mirrors the kernel's arena header and selects shared memory for the first output per channel while retaining inline encoding for later outputs in the step.

nodes.name: _Arena
nodes.summary: Manages a per-channel memory-mapped arena shared with the kernel, checking sequence numbers and capacity while reading and writing payloads.

nodes.name: _InlineAdapter
nodes.summary: Encodes and decodes one inline payload using the protocol's base64 JSON representation.

nodes.name: _ArenaAdapter
nodes.summary: Adapts channel payload encoding and decoding to kernel-owned shared-memory arenas and sequence numbers.

nodes.name: _StepCodec
nodes.summary: Provides the step-scoped transport seam that decodes typed inputs and encodes typed outputs while preserving message order and per-channel transport behavior.

nodes.name: ParticipantFailure
nodes.summary: Exception used to abort participant execution when protocol or transport state is invalid.

nodes.name: Input
nodes.summary: Immutable record containing an input channel, its virtual publish time, and decoded field data.

nodes.name: StepParticipant
nodes.summary: Base participant contract exposing initialization and deterministic step callbacks for subclasses.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Runs the participant JSON-line event loop, initializes schema codecs and arenas, dispatches each step, reports failures, and closes transport resources on shutdown.

nodes.name: _load
nodes.summary: Loads and instantiates a participant class from a file-and-class specification.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Validates the participant CLI argument, loads the requested participant, and starts the protocol loop.

nodes.name: schema.py
nodes.summary: Provides runtime packing and unpacking for schema-defined fixed-layout messages using the same little-endian byte contract as the generated C interface.
nodes.languageNotes: Fixed-size arrays are represented as bytes for u8 elements and lists for other element types, with explicit length checks before packing.

nodes.name: MessageType
nodes.summary: Compiles a schema specification into a struct format and converts typed field dictionaries to and from fixed-layout message bytes.

nodes.name: _Scalar
nodes.summary: Packing plan for a scalar field that maps one Python value to one struct value.

nodes.name: _ByteArray
nodes.summary: Packing plan for fixed-size u8 arrays represented as exact-length byte strings.

nodes.name: _List
nodes.summary: Packing plan for fixed-size non-u8 arrays represented as lists of struct-compatible values.

nodes.name: _field_plan
nodes.summary: Selects the scalar, byte-array, or list packing plan for a schema field.

nodes.name: load
nodes.summary: Constructs a mapping of schema names to compiled MessageType instances.

nodes.name: testing.py
nodes.summary: Pytest-facing frontend that runs a manifest through the SiL runner, converts participant aborts into assertion failures, and decodes recorded channel messages for post-hoc checks.

nodes.name: RunFailure
nodes.summary: AssertionError subclass used to surface a failed simulation run and its participant or runner message to pytest.

nodes.name: participant_command
nodes.summary: Builds the Python module command used to launch a file-defined step participant.

nodes.name: RunResult
nodes.summary: Immutable simulation result wrapper containing the MCAP path, manifest hash, and schema information needed to decode recorded messages.

nodes.name: run_simulation
nodes.summary: Writes a manifest, invokes the configured runner, raises RunFailure on a nonzero exit, and returns typed access to the resulting recording.

nodes.name: ci.yml
nodes.summary: GitHub Actions workflow that runs on pushes to main and pull requests. It provisions a Python environment, builds the C++ kernel with CMake, runs C++ and Python tests, and enforces deterministic reference-pipeline output.
nodes.languageNotes: YAML GitHub Actions workflow with one test job and shell-based build, test, and determinism-gate steps.

nodes.name: config.json
nodes.summary: Controls Understand-Anything output preferences for the project, currently selecting English as the output language.

nodes.name: fingerprints.json
nodes.summary: Stores the versioned content fingerprints and structural-analysis metadata for the 57 files captured at a specific repository commit.

nodes.name: knowledge-graph.json
nodes.summary: Contains the generated sil project knowledge graph, including project metadata, 148 analyzed nodes, 226 relationships, layered organization, and a guided tour.

nodes.name: meta.json
nodes.summary: Records the latest Understand-Anything analysis timestamp, repository commit, tool version, and count of analyzed files.

nodes.name: AGENTS.md
nodes.summary: Repository guidance for coding agents, covering the GitHub issue tracker, triage-label vocabulary, and the locations of domain documentation.

nodes.name: CMakeLists.txt
nodes.summary: CMake build definition for the C++20 SiL kernel, focused tests, virtual clock shim and probe, generated message headers, and toy participant modules. It also fetches nlohmann/json and MCAP as build dependencies.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses CMake FetchContent, custom generation for schema-derived headers, and platform-specific shared-library linking for the clock shim.

nodes.name: CONTEXT.md
nodes.summary: Canonical SiL domain glossary defining virtual-time scheduling terms, participant roles, the step protocol and clock shim, typed channel routing, and reproducibility concepts.

nodes.name: DESIGN.md
nodes.summary: Design decision record for the SiL framework, covering deterministic CI regression runs, the two-tier scheduler, typed pub/sub routing, adapters, manifest and recording contracts, testing, and milestone scope. It also records resolved implementation seams and explicit non-goals.

nodes.name: Makefile
nodes.summary: Developer build and test entry points for creating the Python environment, configuring and building the CMake project, running CTest and pytest, executing manifests, checking determinism, and cleaning generated artifacts.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Project entry-point documentation describing the deterministic scheduling and typed data-routing kernel, milestone-1 features, virtual clock shim, shared-memory transport, build and test commands, repository layout, and deferred capabilities.

nodes.name: domain.md
nodes.summary: Guidance for engineering skills consuming the repository's domain documentation. It defines how to locate context documents and ADRs, use glossary terminology, and surface conflicts with architectural decisions.

nodes.name: issue-tracker.md
nodes.summary: Documents the repository's GitHub issue-tracker workflow, including conventions for issues, pull requests, labels, and wayfinding dependencies. It maps common skill operations to the corresponding gh CLI commands.

nodes.name: triage-labels.md
nodes.summary: Maps the repository's five canonical triage roles to their GitHub label strings and explains the meaning of each label.

nodes.name: .understandignore
nodes.summary: Provides project-specific ignore patterns for Understand-Anything analysis, including build, cache, virtual-environment, and test directories.

nodes.name: scan-result.json
nodes.summary: Stores the scanner's inventory of the sil project, including detected languages, frameworks, file metadata, and resolved import information.

nodes.name: step-protocol.md
nodes.summary: Normative specification for the line-based JSON protocol between the simulation kernel and process participants, including activation messages, outputs, and shared-memory payload handling.

nodes.name: pyproject.toml
nodes.summary: Defines the Python package metadata, Python version requirement, MCAP and development dependencies, sil-check console script, and Hatch wheel layout.

nodes.name: check.py
nodes.summary: Implements the sil-check determinism mode by running a manifest twice, hashing both MCAP recordings, and reporting any byte-level difference.

nodes.name: file_sha256
nodes.summary: Reads a file and returns its SHA-256 digest as a hexadecimal string for deterministic output comparison.

nodes.name: check
nodes.summary: Runs the configured runner twice in a temporary directory, compares the resulting recording hashes, and returns the runner or determinism-violation status.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Parses the sil-check command-line arguments and delegates manifest verification to check.

nodes.name: recording.py
nodes.summary: Provides the Python read-side seam for recorded simulation output, dispatching supported paths to an MCAP message iterator and rejecting unknown extensions.

nodes.name: UnknownRecordingFormat
nodes.summary: ValueError subclass raised when a recording path has an extension that does not identify a supported format.

nodes.name: read_records
nodes.summary: Dispatches a recording path by extension and returns an iterator for MCAP records, raising UnknownRecordingFormat for unsupported formats.

nodes.name: _read_mcap

nodes.name: toy.json

nodes.name: clock_probe.c
nodes.summary: Provides an end-to-end C probe for the clock shim, exercising virtual and realtime clocks, time queries, frozen-step behavior, and non-blocking sleep APIs.
nodes.languageNotes: The probe covers several POSIX clock and sleep entry points and emits key=value results for automated assertions.

nodes.name: main

nodes.name: silschema.py
nodes.summary: Generates packed C message structs and C++ layout assertions from the project's JSON schema format, preserving declared field order and fixed-width types.
nodes.languageNotes: Generated structs use one-byte packing and compile-time C++ size assertions to enforce the shared binary layout.

nodes.name: c_ident
nodes.summary: Converts a dotted schema name into the underscore-separated identifier used for generated C declarations.

nodes.name: member
nodes.summary: Formats one schema field as a C struct member, including fixed-size array syntax when a count is declared.

nodes.name: field_bytes
nodes.summary: Calculates the byte width of a schema field from its primitive type size and optional element count.

nodes.name: generate
nodes.summary: Builds the complete packed C header for all schemas, including struct declarations and C++ static size checks.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Validates command-line arguments, loads a JSON schema, and writes the generated header to the requested output path.

nodes.name: pop
nodes.summary: Removes and returns the front pending message from a subscriber queue while preserving FIFO order.

nodes.name: push
nodes.summary: Appends a pending message to a subscriber queue in publish order.

nodes.name: now_ns
nodes.summary: Returns the engine's current stepped virtual time in nanoseconds.

nodes.name: in_setup
nodes.summary: Reports whether the engine is currently accepting setup-time participant operations.

nodes.name: in_task

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to understand SiL's purpose: a deterministic software-in-the-loop kernel focused on virtual-time scheduling and typed data routing. It introduces the one-run manifest workflow, native and process participants, MCAP recordings, the virtual clock shim, and shared-memory transport that the rest of this tour will trace.

tour.title: Runner Entry Point
tour.description: The sil-run CLI is the runtime front door. Building on the workflow described in Step 1, this entry point parses the manifest and output path, chooses the recording sink, starts the engine, and translates configuration, runtime, and determinism failures into meaningful exit codes.
tour.languageLesson: C++ entry points commonly keep orchestration thin: main() wires together long-lived subsystems while domain behavior remains in focused classes such as Manifest, Engine, and the recording adapters.

tour.title: Manifest and Message Contract
tour.description: The manifest turns a declarative JSON run description into typed kernel configuration, while the toy schema and code generator establish the byte-level message contract shared by C++ and Python. This is the foundation for deterministic routing: schemas define what a payload means, and the manifest defines which channels and participants exist.

tour.title: Virtual-Time Engine
tour.description: The Engine is the center of the architecture identified by the dependency analysis. It registers participant tasks, advances virtual time, publishes messages through channel queues, applies interceptor plans, and exposes deterministic take/fail operations; the interceptor files make fault injection an explicit, ordered part of publication rather than hidden participant behavior.
tour.languageLesson: The C++ headers define narrow seams and state types, while the .cpp files supply behavior. This separation makes the scheduler and its invariants easier to inspect without exposing implementation details to adapters.

tour.title: Native Participant ABI
tour.description: Native participants plug into the Engine through the stable C ABI, which exposes task registration, subscriptions, publication, virtual time, and failure reporting without coupling shared libraries to C++ internals. The toy producer and accumulator make the flow concrete: one emits typed counters and the other consumes them to publish accumulated state.

tour.title: Process Step Protocol
tour.description: For opaque or separately launched vECUs, the process adapter translates Engine queues into the normative JSON-lines step protocol and translates participant outputs back into channel publications. The protocol document explains the observable contract, while the arena and mapped-region files support the shared-memory path when inline base64 transport would dominate runtime cost.

tour.title: Virtual Clock Shim
tour.description: The clock-shim path preserves determinism for unchanged POSIX vECUs that read wall-clock APIs. The kernel-side resolver and process setup publish frozen virtual time through the shared clock region, while the preload library interposes clock and sleep calls; the probe demonstrates the boundary and its expected behavior.

tour.title: Recording and Replay
tour.description: After messages are routed, the format-neutral recording seam lets the Engine preserve total publish order without depending on a particular file format. The MCAP implementation records schemas and payloads, the replayer injects timestamped messages back through the same Engine publication path, and SHA-256 helpers verify that manifests and recordings match the deterministic run they represent.

tour.title: Python Frontend
tour.description: The Python package gives callers and process participants a productive front end to the C++ contracts established in earlier steps. Its manifest builder emits canonical execution inputs, schema.py packs and unpacks the same fixed layouts, and participant.py implements the step lifecycle and both payload transports for Python vECUs.
tour.languageLesson: Python's small adapter classes and public re-exports create a convenient API without changing the wire contract. The important boundary is serialization: Python objects become the same deterministic little-endian bytes consumed by the kernel.

tour.title: Testing and Determinism
tour.description: The testing frontend runs manifests at the simulation boundary, turns in-simulation participant failures into pytest failures, and reads recorded channels for assertions. The check command then runs the same manifest twice and compares the resulting MCAP bytes, making determinism an executable property rather than a documentation claim; package metadata exposes that command to users.

tour.title: Build and Developer Workflow
tour.description: CMakeLists.txt describes how the C++20 kernel, generated message headers, shim, probes, and toy libraries are assembled, while the Makefile provides the repeatable commands developers use to build, test, run manifests, and invoke the determinism check. Together they connect the source layers from Steps 3-10 to a reproducible local workflow.
tour.languageLesson: Make targets are named workflow commands, not necessarily files. Phony targets and dependency ordering let a short command such as a test or check target coordinate several build and verification tools.

tour.title: Architecture and CI Capstone
tour.description: DESIGN.md records why the framework is split into a deterministic kernel, explicit adapters, typed channels, and format-neutral recording seams, while CONTEXT.md supplies the vocabulary needed to discuss those boundaries precisely. The CI workflow is the capstone: it builds the complete system, runs C++ and Python tests, and enforces the reference determinism proof described throughout the tour.
